scope: branch quant/canonical-price-integrity-d1-d2 vs origin/main; core 1.2.0 run 38772238376

findings.finding: The audit's false-positive measure is not independent of the detector, and an independent SEC-share-count label shows a materially higher false-positive rate than the 1.2.0 rationale claims.
evidence: scripts/quant/price-integrity-audit.mjs:273-277: falsePositiveCandidate = !(plausible && persistsOrSpike); SEC share count is not decisive, persistence alone clears a hold.

quant/engines/price-integrity.js explainDay: 'if (up && match && (sig || ...))' -> cause UNDECLARED_REVERSE_SPLIT whenever the core signature fires; confidence HIGH for sig && persists, regardless of secSharesRatio.

Independent label on rebuild.newHolds (SPLIT_SUSPECTED_UNDECLARED, n=90): 58 no SEC evidence; of 32 with SEC evidence: 13 SPLIT (shares x k within x1.5), 5 LEAN_SPLIT (shares x k <= 3), 14 CONTRADICTED (shares fell far less than 1/k), 5 of them with shares unchanged within +-1%.
Only 7 of the 14 contradicted holds carry falsePositiveCandidate=true; one hold with a ~25x jump and SEC share ratio 1.000 is labelled UNDECLARED_REVERSE_SPLIT/HIGH.
Contradicted by path: VOLUME_INVERSE 9/18 SEC-evidenced, EXACT_RATIO_OVERNIGHT 4/13, OUT_OF_RANGE 1/1.
Commit e049f4c claims 2/11 false for k>=5 in 1.1.0; for 1.2.0 the independent rate is 16% (strict, shares unchanged) to 44% (broad) of SEC-evidenced holds.
findings.harm: Genuine series are truncated as HOLD and the published acceptance metric (falsePositiveCandidates=35) understates this, so a calibration start would rest on a non-independent quality claim.
findings.recommendation: Define FP/TP solely by an independent label (SEC shares ratio vs 1/k, pre-registered tolerance) and report precision with CI per path; never let forensic cause derive from CTR.undeclaredReverseSplitSignature. Set a pre-registered acceptance threshold for precision before re-running.

findings.finding: The k>=5 floor of 1.2.0 leaks: the +-25% tolerance lets raw ratios 4.0-5.0 match k=5.
evidence: canonical-total-return.js undeclaredReverseSplitSignature: conventional = best <= log(1.25); |log(4/5)| == log(1.25) so an exact 4.0x passes as k=5.
14 of 90 SPLIT_SUSPECTED_UNDECLARED holds have raw close ratio < 5 (4 of them exactly 4.0x); of the 3 with SEC evidence, 2 are contradicted (shares unchanged / rising).
findings.harm: Re-admits exactly the k<5 sub-penny tick-move class that 1.1.0 failed on.
findings.recommendation: Make the floor explicit (rawRatio >= k_min / small tolerance) or narrow the tolerance at the floor; pre-register.

findings.finding: EXACT_RATIO_OVERNIGHT premise ('a market move does not land exactly on 10.00x') fails for tick-quantized sub-cent prices; this path ignores volume.
evidence: 27 of 51 exact-path holds have a sub-cent prior close, where one-tick moves produce exact integer ratios.
4 of 13 SEC-evidenced exact-path holds are contradicted; one forensically STALE_PRICE hold at exactly 5x has SEC share ratio 1.001.
findings.harm: Illiquid sub-cent names are held as splits on tick noise.
findings.recommendation: Require exactness to be resolvable above tick granularity (prior close >= N ticks) or require volume evidence for the exact path at low price levels.

findings.area: 2 false-negative split detection / residual extreme returns
findings.finding: Large residual of undeclared extreme raw jumps remains inside canonical-valid bars; several SEC-confirmed reverse splits still pass as returns; no detection at all for the downward direction.
evidence: QUANT-PRICE-INTEGRITY-REBUILD.json corporateActionConsistency.undeclared10xJumpsInsideCanonicalBars.after = 188 (190 under 1.1.0).

known83: 48/83 still extreme (UNRESOLVED 12, UNDECLARED_REVERSE_SPLIT 4, DECLARED_SPLIT_INCONSISTENT 1, DECLARED_SPLIT_DATE_SHIFT 1, GENUINE_PRICE_MOVE 30). All 2213: still-extreme with defect cause UNRESOLVED 21, UNDECLARED_REVERSE_SPLIT 7, STALE 3, UNIT 1, DATE_SHIFT 1, INCONSISTENT 1.
Golden G-KNOWN-FN-10.3X: SEC confirms ~1:11, volume 0.40x > 3/k -> passes as a >+1000% month (authors label it a blocker).
An overnight ~1115x jump with day volume 1.04x of median passes (OUT_OF_RANGE path requires volume < median).

k-selection defect: k is chosen as nearest to the close only, then open is tested against that k. Cases 23.5x close / 19.7x open (both within 25% of k=20; SEC shares fell ~7.5x) and 148x / 236x (SEC shares fell ~70x) are rejected.

Raw census: 296 >=10x downward daily jumps (UNRESOLVED 145, FORWARD_SPLIT_POSSIBLE 35, CURRENCY_OR_UNIT 33, PROVIDER_SPIKE 36 ...); the core returns null for r<1 except reverted spikes (PI18 documents this).
findings.harm: +900% / -90% one-day moves that are data errors stay in the canonical dataset and dominate tail statistics (momentum, volatility, drawdown) of any calibration.
findings.recommendation: Choose k minimizing max(|log(close/k)|,|log(open/k)|); add a frozen down-direction/unit rule (HOLD on >=10x moves with forward-split or unit signature, or SEC-confirmed); use SEC shares, when available at t, as a confirming path; report residual count inside the intended calibration universe.

findings.finding: Of 74 securities with split-adjusted level > 1e6, 13 carry a defect cause; 11 of those remain canonical without any core quarantine. Only 1 was newly quarantined by the fix.
evidence: rebuild.highLevelFate: UNDECLARED_JUMP_IN_HISTORY 9 unquarantined (first jump cause: 6 forward-split-possible, 2 unresolved, 1 date shift), DECLARED_SPLIT_INCONSISTENT 2 unquarantined, both V4 SPLIT_ARTIFACT, core state TOTAL_RETURN_RECONSTRUCTED.
Core event band 0.4..2.5 accepts declared-split-day gross 2.0-2.5 that the forensic (and V4 band 2) call inconsistent.
V4 price-sanity-v4 cuts SPLIT_ARTIFACT downstream, but classifies 10-50x undeclared jumps as GENUINE (UNIT_JUMP_RATIO=50); quant consumers have no such layer.
findings.harm: Known, located fake jumps and inconsistent split days remain in the canonical data; the D2 claim (no blanket cap, cause-based handling) is right in principle but incomplete in effect.
findings.recommendation: Quarantine these from the defect event by a frozen cause-based rule in the core (align core event band with the forensic band or HOLD on inconsistent split days); re-measure.

findings.finding: HOLD is effectively permanent and in V4 becomes a DATA_QUARANTINE terminal whose handling is outcome-correlated; no classical survivorship (valid prefix kept), but informative censoring.
evidence: No confirmation path exists in canonical-total-return.js (no override/allowlist); 'until a corporate-action source confirms' is not implemented.

data.mjs:267-281 slices raw at the event, terminal kind DATA_QUARANTINE; runner.mjs:147 censors any signal horizon containing it; accounting.mjs:81-88 settles at last pre-event close x scenario factor.
runner.mjs:104 injects the terminal bar with rawClose: Infinity, so the DISTRESS_ZERO scenario test rawClose<1 can never fire; 89 of 106 new holds have a sub-dollar prior close.
Bars removed 87,790 (~830 per hold); DELISTED terminals 3195->3156 replaced by DATA_QUARANTINE (proceeds treatment changes).
findings.harm: Reverse splits are distress events; censoring their forward windows biases signal-level forward returns upward for strategies selecting distressed names; distress-scenario sensitivity is understated.
findings.recommendation: Normalize SEC-confirmed cases instead of holding; pre-register censoring counts by reason and a worst-case treatment of DATA_QUARANTINE in sensitivity; carry lastRawClose in the injected bar (separate V4 PR).

findings.finding: Split signature is causal (bars <= t; observedAt == from for all 90). PRICE_SPIKE_REVERTED is detected at t+1 but quarantined from t, and the V4 consumer keys eligibility and settlement on terminal.date, not observedAt: one-session look-ahead. A single reverted bad tick also ends the series permanently.
evidence: 16 holds with observedAt = from + 1 session, all PRICE_SPIKE_REVERTED.
data.mjs:382 and :461 'terminal.date > asOf' excludes the security on the spike day; accounting.mjs:84 settles on terminal.date.
canonical-total-return.js revertedSpike returns date of bar i-1; reconstruct returns UNAVAILABLE for everything after, although the series is valid after the revert.
findings.harm: A backtest removes a security on the day its bad tick appears, using information from the next day; a live system could not. Small (16 securities), but categorical.
findings.recommendation: Invalidate only the spike bar (or use observedAt for eligibility/settlement) and continue the series after the revert; test with a prefix ending on the spike day.

findings.finding: V4 coverage loss is modest, but outside V4 a hold removes the whole total-return history, and this was not measured.
evidence: scripts/quant/lib/daily-prices.mjs:56: tr = ctr.reconstructed ? ... : null; whole-series unavailability (no prefix) for signal/setup backtests, survivorship control; also used by scripts/market/refresh-benchmark-history.mjs and scripts/vorsorge/ingest-tiingo-etfs.mjs.

Fixture evidence in quant/tests/total-return-contract.test.mjs and benchmark-reference.test.mjs: one decades-old undeclared event removes a published long series from the study (titles 58->57, TR coverage 93.3%->91.7%).
CLAUDE.md: changes to quant models need their own PR with a before/after comparison; none exists for these consumers.
findings.harm: Quant products lose entire histories (with an FP rate of 16-44% on SEC-evidenced holds), and the published studies change without a measured comparison.
findings.recommendation: Either adopt prefix semantics in daily-prices (as V4 does) or gate the new reasons behind an opt-in for non-V4 consumers; produce the before/after for quant consumers.

findings.finding: No extreme cases on reused listings; HOLD is a safe outcome, but some holds may be listing events mislabelled as splits.
evidence: extremeCases reusedLater: 0 of 2213.
6 holds follow a 10-29 day gap (below the 30-day segment split).

16 core-signature days in the raw census fall on LISTING_CHANGE (>30 day gap) days; in quant consumers without 30-day segmentation they would be labelled SPLIT_SUSPECTED_UNDECLARED rather than LISTING_DISCONTINUITY.
findings.recommendation: Give listing gaps precedence over the signature; record gapDays in the core result.

findings.finding: Unit changes are accepted (policy CURRENCY_OR_UNIT -> UNRESOLVED_PRICE_DISCONTINUITY -> ACCEPT); there is no core rule for them, and no currency check in the core.
evidence: Raw census: 39 unit-ratio jumps (33 down >=10x).
1 extreme -99% month still extreme with cause CURRENCY_OR_UNIT.
All extremes are on US exchanges; no non-USD evidence.
findings.harm: A 100x unit change passes as a -99% return.
findings.recommendation: Fold into the R4 down-direction rule; pre-register.

findings.finding: Holds on stale series carry split/spike reason codes, and the volume test is weak on illiquid series.
evidence: 13 holds forensically STALE_PRICE (>=5 stale bars before the jump) carry SPLIT_SUSPECTED_UNDECLARED (12) or PRICE_SPIKE_REVERTED (1).
Volume median uses only volume>0 bars and reaches back arbitrarily far.
findings.recommendation: Check stale runs before the signature and use a STALE reason; bound the volume look-back in calendar time.

findings.finding: No dependency on strategy or performance results found.
evidence: Audit imports only capture/measurement/diagnostic modules; public JSON performanceCalculated:false, calibrationRun:false.

Thresholds are ratio/volume constants. The case population was selected via monthly EW_MARKET holding returns >100% (a benchmark construction, not a strategy); the rules are signature-based, not return-size based.
findings.recommendation: Keep it that way: no threshold change after any calibration output is seen.

findings.finding: The 1.1.0->1.2.0 revision is partly justified by independent evidence (k=2/3 SEC-contradicted 51/53), but it is in-sample and not a pure tightening: two new detection paths were added after seeing the 83 cases, and the forensic labeler that defines the evaluation was changed at the same time.
evidence: git diff dbb9aba e049f4c: undeclaredSplitOutOfRange (>=100x) and undeclaredSplitExact (2%) paths added; persistence rule and an intraday-squeeze GENUINE rule added to explainDay.
Goldens are drawn from the audit cases (e.g. G-D1-EXACT-40X 'from the 83 list').
Same data, different labels: in83 root causes UNDECLARED_REVERSE_SPLIT 16->23, UNRESOLVED 32->20, GENUINE 26->32 between runs.
No correlation or performance used (confirmed in code).
findings.harm: Detector and its yardstick were co-tuned on the same population, so resolution rates (35/83 by NEW_HOLD) are optimistic.
findings.recommendation: Freeze the rules; measure precision/recall on a held-out label set (SEC-labelled jumps not in the 83, or a held-out period) with a pre-registered pass threshold; decouple the forensic labeler from the core.

findings.finding: Stale version strings and an inconsistent public census.
evidence: price-integrity.js header says price-integrity-1.0.0 / corporate-action-contract-1.1.0 while VERSION=price-integrity-1.1.0 and contract 1.2.0; CONFIG comments say 1.1.0.
dailyRawJumpCensus.total 2566 (canonical-prefix bars) vs byCause sum 2839 (all raw bars including quarantined suffixes), mixed in one object.
findings.recommendation: Fix the labels and state both denominators.

evidence: node --test quant/tests/price-integrity.test.mjs quant/tests/canonical-total-return.test.mjs: 53/53 pass; full quant/tests: 2825/2825 pass.
git diff origin/main...HEAD: no files under quant/data, discover/data, supertrader/data, social/data.
No blanket price cap: core has none; 1e6 appears only in the forensic explainHighLevel; test PI11 (400k nominal) passes.
Workflow follows ADR-005 (ref github.ref, push-with-retry, ref_name concurrency, top-level contents: read, set -euo pipefail).
Public JSON files contain no tickers or segment IDs. Note: a test comment and a commit message name one public fixture security.

findings.finding: The V4 price-sanity layer that still runs after the core only applies its defect checks to securities whose maximum split-adjusted level over the full history exceeds 1e6. That level depends on future reverse splits.
evidence: price-sanity-v4.mjs classifyPriceLevel: returns null unless max(close) > 1e6 over all bars; adjusted closes are back-propagated from later splits; called in loadPrepared before the calibration.
findings.harm: Whether a defect at time t is quarantined depends on corporate actions after t (look-ahead-conditioned data cleaning).
findings.recommendation: Retire the level-conditioned layer in favor of the core's cause-based rules applied to all securities, or apply its defect checks unconditionally; declare it in the new protocol.

verdict.summary: 1.2.0 removes the most egregious undeclared reverse splits causally, without a price cap and without performance input, and V4 coverage loss is small (0.6% of bars). But it is not yet clean enough to start a new pre-registered calibration.
remainingBlockers: B1 (R1,R13): freeze the rules and measure precision/recall against an independent SEC label on a held-out set with a pre-registered threshold; current independent FP rate on SEC-evidenced holds is 16-44%.

B2 (R4,R10): 188 undeclared >=10x jumps remain inside canonical bars; add a frozen down-direction/unit rule and fix the open/close k-selection defect, or pre-register a calibration universe that provably excludes them, and report the residual count inside that universe.
B3 (R5): quarantine the 11 known D2 defect securities via a cause-based core rule.
B4 (R7,R16): remove the one-session spike look-ahead (use observedAt or invalidate only the bad bar) and the level-conditioned V4 price-sanity selection, or declare them in the protocol.
B5 (R6): pre-register DATA_QUARANTINE censoring and settlement handling, including the rawClose:Infinity distress gap.
nonBlockingButMergeRelevant: R8: whole-series total-return loss in quant consumers needs a before/after comparison or prefix semantics before merge.
